title: Finite-Tor and witnessed domains for all relative-product factors
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, integers $a,n\geq1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^a}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, and fix the six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] for these parameters. Integral pullbacks and tensors are completed; field coefficients use rationalization and a common finite coefficient field. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $f:X\to B$ and $g:Y\to B$ be separated finite-type morphisms, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Write $T=X\times_BY$, $u:T\to X$, $v:T\to Y$, $h=fu=gv$, $P=Lu^*K$, $Q=Rf_!K$ and $H=P\otimes^L_\Lambda Lv^*L$. Then $X,Y,T$ are separated finite type over $k$, and $u,v,h$ are separated finite type. The objects
$$P,\ Lv^*L,\ H\quad\text{on }T,\qquad Q\quad\text{on }B,$$
$$Rv_!P,\ Lg^*Q,\ Rv_!P\otimes^L L,\ Lg^*Q\otimes^L L,\ L\otimes^L Lg^*Q\quad\text{on }Y$$
belong to the indicated $D^b_{ctf}$ categories. Their compact-support images on $B$, and the tensors $Rg_!L\otimes^L Q$ and $Q\otimes^L Rg_!L$, also belong to $D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda)$. Thus both projection components at $(v,P,L)$ and $(g,L,Q)$ have finite-Tor second argument. At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ every displayed bounded constructible pro-etale input admits an etale-origin witness: it is isomorphic to the pullback of a bounded constructible etale complex under the comparison of sites. In particular $H$ and $K$ lie in the witnessed domains of the finite compact-support composition and exchange. At $\mathcal O_E$ the corresponding witnesses exist for each finite reduction in the derived-complete coefficient construction. At $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ the operations and these finite witnesses are formed from integral presentations, after choosing a common finite coefficient field for the objects involved. These assertions concern the completed and transported coefficient categories, not discrete non-torsion etale coefficients. The same domain assertions apply to every other pair of separated finite-type maps into a separated finite-type base and every pair of finite-Tor inputs.

Transport its etale origin isomorphism across the canonical realization equivalence, using mapDerivedCategoryCompIso, and retain the bounded-below image F, its FixedEtaleOriginWitness and the comparison to the inverse realization. For every positive reduction, integral constructibility already supplies bounded intrinsic constructibility. Apply the preceding finite-origin argument separately at each level. Thus every integral object in the displayed stage list has both required properties, without extra assumptions on its position in that list.

proof.text: The private stage_presented lemma compares the exact 22-object lists through any supplied coefficient comparison with its tensor comparison. For pullback and support it composes the comparison component with the image of the previously obtained isomorphism; for tensor it composes the tensor comparison with the mapped product of the two input isomorphisms. Assemble these into List.Forall₂ with reflexive scheme labels. At rational coefficients take the raw localization’s actual integral input objects K.obj and L.obj, apply the integral argument to the entire list and use the supplied rationalization and rationalExchangeComparison.tensor.

proof.text: At algebraically closed coefficients take the finite compositum of K.stage and L.stage and their actual transported objects Kr and Lr. Their underlying objects are integral representatives because rationalization is raw. Apply the previous list comparison first to integral-to-rational passage in this coefficient stage, then to the commonStageComparison and commonStageExchangeComparison.tensor, with the canonical isoToStage isomorphisms of K and L. The private presented_trans proof composes the two Forall₂ relations entrywise. Apply the integral argument at this coefficient field to provide all finite witnesses.
